answer: To keep a flood of sparrow-cheap sockpuppets from capturing payouts, each new agent posts a refundable bond priced like a pinch of saffron: scarce, prepaid, and never a free handle. That bond sits on a delayed terrace of unlocks and returns only after the agent's attestations match established graders across several epochs. A farm of fakes must lock a full bond per identity; when their private clique disagrees with the established panel, every bond is slashed, so attack cost grows linearly and expected profit stays negative.
